items.q: An investment costs £480,000. Net cash flows are Year 1: £150,000; Year 2: £100,000; Year 3: £70,000; Year 4: £120,000; Year 5: £50,000. What is the payback period?
items.why: After 4 years the cumulative cash flow is £440,000, so £40,000 is still needed. In year 5 the business receives £50,000, about £4,167 a month. £40,000 ÷ £50,000 × 12 = 9.6, so about 10 months. Payback = 4 years 10 months.
items.label: New question

items.q: 8.7 million people worked at least partly from home in 2019. In 2020, 36% of the 32.5 million people in employment did so. Calculate the percentage change in the number working at least partly from home.
items.label: Paper 2 June 2023 Q02.1

items.q: Revenue rose by 8% to £205.2m. What was revenue before the rise?
items.why: £205.2m is 108% of the original. Original = £205.2m ÷ 1.08 = £190m. Taking 8% off £205.2m gives the wrong answer, because the 8% was worked out on the smaller original figure.
items.label: New question

items.q: A product has an income elasticity of demand of -1.2. Average real incomes rise by 4%. What happens to demand?
items.why: % change in demand = YED × % change in income = -1.2 × +4% = -4.8%. A negative YED means an inferior good: demand moves the opposite way to income.
items.label: New question

items.q: A business has revenue of £1,056,000, cost of sales of £660,000 and payables of £100,000. What are its payables days?
items.why: Payables days = payables ÷ cost of sales × 365 = £100,000 ÷ £660,000 × 365 = 55.3, about 55 days. Payables days use cost of sales, not revenue.
items.label: New question

items.q: Product X: fixed costs £8,000, selling price £10, variable costs £6 per unit, total contribution from the current level of output £10,000. Calculate the margin of safety.
items.why: Contribution per unit = £10 – £6 = £4. Current output = £10,000 ÷ £4 = 2,500 units. Break-even = £8,000 ÷ £4 = 2,000 units. Margin of safety = 2,500 – 2,000 = 500 units.
items.label: Paper 1 June 2024 Q16

items.q: A business has capacity utilisation of 60%. It increases its capacity by 50% while output stays the same. What is its new capacity utilisation?
items.why: Take capacity as 100 units: output is 60. New capacity = 150. Utilisation = 60 ÷ 150 × 100 = 40%.
items.label: New question

items.q: A company invests £20 million in Year 0. Net returns: Year 1 £11m (discount factor 0.91), Year 2 £12m (discount factor 0.83). Calculate the expected net present value.
items.why: Present values: £11m × 0.91 = £10.01m; £12m × 0.83 = £9.96m. Total = £19.97m. NPV = £19.97m – £20m = –£0.03m (–£30,000). A negative NPV, even though the returns add up to more than £20m.
items.label: Paper 1 June 2024 Q17

items.q: Opening balance £5,000 on 1 July. Cash outflow £14,000. Net cash flow for July = £22,000. Closing balance on 31 July?
items.why: If net cash flow = £22,000 and outflow = £14,000, then cash inflow = 22,000 + 14,000 = £36,000. Closing balance = opening + net cash flow = 5,000 + 22,000 = £27,000. Students sometimes subtract instead of add. Closing balance = Opening balance + Net cash flow.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: The chart shows a business's inventory over time. How many units does the business use each day?
items.why: Inventory falls from 350 to 100 units, a fall of 250 units, over 5 days. 250 ÷ 5 = 50 units a day.
items.label: New question
